passages.original: Ita igitur propter u am substantiam Sabellius tres noluit fateri personas, sicut e contra- rio Arius propter tres personas, tres voluit prædirare substantias. Apostolica sane Ecclesia tres personas contra Sabellium numerans, unam vero subsitantiam vel essentiam contra Arium vindicans, ita dictum sibi meminit :Audi, Israel, Dominus Deus tuus, Deus unus esi (Deut. VI, 4); ut hic unus Deus non sit solilarius, sed Trinius, Pater scilicet, Filius, et Spiritus sanctus. Qua confessione prælata, magnum pietatis et mirabile sacramentum (/ Tim.
passages.english: So, then, on account of the one substance Sabellius refused to confess three persons, just as, on the contrary, Arius on account of the three persons wished to proclaim three substances. The apostolic Church, indeed, counting three persons against Sabellius, and upholding one substance or essence against Arius, remembers that it was told: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God is one God" (Deut. 6:4), in such a way that this one God is not solitary but threefold, namely Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Having set forth this confession, [we come to] the great and wonderful mystery of godliness (1 Tim.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'u am' read as 'unam', 'prædirare' as 'prædicare', 'subsitantiam' as 'substantiam', 'esi' as 'est', 'solilarius' as 'solitarius'. 'Trinius' is taken as 'trinus' (threefold). The last sentence is incomplete here; its main verb ('pandentes', 'revealing') comes in the following context, so '[we come to]' is supplied only to bridge the break.
